title: Marionette: Fine-Grained Conditional Generative Modeling of Spatiotemporal Human Trajectory Data Beyond Imitation

problem.claim: Human trajectory data generation needs to account for rich mobility context that can affect human mobility patterns.

gap.claim: Recent neural generative models mostly use unconditional, purely data-driven imitative learning and do not consider social events, weather, or other rich mobility contexts.

contributions.claim: Marionette is a manipulatable generative model for human trajectory data with fine-grained conditions.
The model integrates global and partial mobility-related contexts and extracts sequence-level and event-level conditions.
It uses cascading conditioning mechanisms with diffusion-alike Temporal Point Processes and discrete diffusion models to model temporal and spatial dynamics.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On two real-world human trajectory datasets, Marionette reportedly outperforms the best baselines by 13.96–54.13% on statistical and distributional similarity metrics.
The authors report improvements of 9.36–40.63% in task-based data utility evaluation.
Ablation studies reportedly verify key design choices, and case studies demonstrate generation in previously unseen scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Synthetic human trajectory data is increasingly used in urban planning, traffic control, and crowd monitoring.
Existing neural generative models largely imitate data unconditionally without modeling rich mobility context.
Marionette introduces fine-grained conditional generation using global and partial contexts, sequence-level and event-level conditions, and cascading temporal and spatial conditioning.
The authors evaluate Marionette on two real-world datasets against many baselines and report gains on similarity and utility metrics.
Ablations and case studies are reported as supporting the design choices and manipulability in unseen scenarios.

source_observation.claim: The model conditions trajectory generation on both global and partial mobility contexts.

interpretation.claim: Separating context scope may support more targeted control of generated spatiotemporal behavior.

application.claim: Applications requiring scenario-specific trajectory synthesis could expose controls for broad conditions and localized events.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which conditions are most effective or how control quality varies across scenarios.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two trajectory datasets.
The specific baselines, metrics, conditions, and unseen scenarios are not described.
Training, computational, and reproducibility details are omitted.
